subject.title: unsafe plugin path error after onboarding

question: Should openclaw-ansible fix this by changing the default release install/trusted-path behavior, or should it rely on upstream OpenClaw packaging plus an optional version-pinning mitigation?
rationale: The observed failure is at the boundary between installer package layout and OpenClaw plugin path validation, and choosing npm/pnpm behavior, trusted roots, or release pinning changes install policy rather than a purely mechanical repo-local bug fix.

options.title: Verify and fix installer path
options.body: Run a fresh Ubuntu install first, then change the release install path or config generation only if current `latest` still produces unsafe bundled plugin paths.

options.title: Defer to upstream packaging
options.body: Keep this issue open until upstream OpenClaw confirms the package layout no longer triggers the validator and close only with fresh install proof.

options.title: Use version pinning as mitigation
options.body: Adopt https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-ansible/pull/50 as a mitigation for bad upstream releases while leaving the default `latest` behavior unchanged unless maintainers later change policy.

recommendation.title: Verify and fix installer path
recommendation.body: Run a fresh Ubuntu install first, then change the release install path or config generation only if current `latest` still produces unsafe bundled plugin paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The current OpenClaw release package path and docs trace most directly to this rename-era installer history.
